facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s was brought to the emergency department after she collapsed
received chest compressions from her husband, and recovered consciousness at home
On admission, the patient was conscious without any discomfort
Vital signs were normal
physical examination was unremarkable
12-lead ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals
repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block/left axis deviation–like morphology and short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds
Continuous ECG monitoring revealed recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, some deteriorating into ventricular fibrillation
Serum electrolyte levels were normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure
Emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease
Revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)

concepts.why: The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes and recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which are characteristic of CPVT, and the genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2), which is often associated with CPVT.

The patient's ECG monitoring revealed recurrent episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia deteriorating into ventricular fibrillation, and the emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease, which are consistent with IVF.

The patient's 12-lead ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals, and repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block/left axis deviation–like morphology, which can be seen in ERS.

The patient's ECG showed normal QT intervals, but the genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2), which can be associated with LQTS, although the normal QT interval makes this less likely.

The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with atypical left bundle-branch block/left axis deviation–like morphology, which can be seen in BS, although the absence of characteristic ST-segment elevation in the right precordial leads makes this less likely.
